questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/797cddb4ea3cb41959df88e56517e9ee71e76e3cd08a9a93d2957b9792d14abb.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=-\frac{2x}{3},$ $y=\frac{4x}{3}$ and $y=\frac{x}{3}+3,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
questions.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/0e69b1cb480b87216273db4336adff57cbf9d9bc450aac4b0cdb58b1ae63f6f7.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-3\le x\le 0,\,-\frac{2x}{3}\le y\le \frac{x}{3}+3}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\frac{4x}{3}\le y\le \frac{x}{3}+3}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}{\int }_{-2x/3}^{x/3+3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{4x/3}^{x/3+3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/a4515d2789a9b5c7a08210c0ef2611e7b6e661850b1fa822016b880427088bae.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y={x}^{2},$ and the lines $y=2-x$ and $y=x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y={x}^{2} & \,⟹\,x=-\sqrt{y} \\ y=2-x & \,⟹\,x=2-y \\ y=x & \,⟹\,x=y\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/78aa61f11856dbf35287a0af016b56744fec354d6c4e64690a1a6fe466f164e8.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,-\sqrt{y}\le x\le y}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 4,\,-\sqrt{y}\le x\le 2-y}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-\sqrt{y}}^{y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{-\sqrt{y}}^{2-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=x+6,$ $y=2x,$ and $y=3x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2} \\ y=x+6 & \,⟹\,x=y-6 \\ y=3x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{3}\end{aligned}

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/c453d46a1f0cd6e6ddfa926de471fe38663df2bd86b9cdf4e58ce8d42462774a.png)

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 9,\,\frac{y}{3}\le x\le \frac{y}{2}}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,9\le y\le 12,\,y-6\le x\le \frac{y}{2}}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{9}{\int }_{y/3}^{y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{9}^{12}{\int }_{y-6}^{y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=-x,$ $y=6-4x$ and $y=2x.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=-x & \,⟹\,x=-y \\ y=6-4x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4} \\ y=2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/08237d1ca2e01d0cf620dfa06a4265d8053b7ee34d0b65036aad7d5734726e1c.png)

 

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/c756dc7924fc4c116601da907eb3b767b8a40647e063c146dad83b0ea660933b.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-y\le x\le \frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4}}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le \frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4}}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-y}^{3/2-y/4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y/2}^{3/2-y/4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Double Integral Over a Partitioned Region
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's draw a sketch of our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/c9072d2b8f1b49770403280af13d3d8e681247f168e796c056eb697fe28b8ba9.png)

  

The  region $D={(x,y)|\,\,|x-1|+|y|\le 1}$ can be  partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/d16296029378c7adb891affba63683971ff972b5ed0268641ac3b677c694b5f8.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,y\le x\le 2-y}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,-y\le x\le y+2}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{|x-1|+|y|\le 1}6(x+y)^{2}\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}6(x+y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}6(x+y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y}^{2-y}6(x+y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{-y}^{y+2}6(x+y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[3(x+y)^{2}]_{y}^{2-y}\text{d}y+{\int }_{-1}^{0}[3(x+y)^{2}]_{-y}^{y+2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3(4-4{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{-1}^{0}3(2y+2)^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =3{[4y-\frac{4{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{1}+4{[(y+1)^{3}]}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =8+4 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate ${∬}_{D}2y\,dA,$ where $D$ is the region shown in the picture above.
questions.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/33a38da74b282f0ec1fb2fae9cb155feb2a5fd39128c7607b80c6b84fedd29b4.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,x-1\le y\le 3-x}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 4,\,3-x\le y\le x-1}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2y\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}2y\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}2y\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{x-1}^{3-x}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{3-x}^{x-1}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,{|}_{x-1}^{3-x}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{y}^{2}\,{|}_{3-x}^{x-1}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[(3-x)^{2}-(x-1)^{2}]\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}[(x-1)^{2}-(3-x)^{2}]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(8-4x)\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}(4x-8)\text{d}x \\  & =(8x-2{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{2}+(2{x}^{2}-8x){|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =8(2-1)-2({2}^{2}-{1}^{2})+2({4}^{2}-{2}^{2})-8(4-2) \\  & =8-6+24-16 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le -x}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x}.
$$

 

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2x\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}2x\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}2x\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{-x}2x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x}2x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}2xy{|}_{{x}^{2}}^{-x}\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}2xy{|}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}2x[-x-{x}^{2}]\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}2x[x-{x}^{2}]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(-2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}]}_{-1}^{0}+{[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =((0-(-\frac{2}{3}(-1)^{3}-\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{4}))+((\frac{2}{3}(1)^{3}-\frac{1}{2}(1)^{4})-0)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/ebb0b09ffab6ffdff6a04104b09d6904302fdb7580262663b5e0c65bd3f95502.png)

The region $D$ is enclosed by the the curve $y=(x-1)^{2}$ and the lines $y=x+1$ and $y=3-x,$ as shown in the picture. Evaluate ${∬}_{D}2y\,dA.$
questions.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/f26c3e1bbbc268308db8d419bc799ad5349673e97c8828471997a5d36cb94d7d.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,(x-1)^{2}\le y\le x+1}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,(x-1)^{2}\le y\le 3-x}.
$$

 

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2y\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}2y\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}2y\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{(x-1)^{2}}^{x+1}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{(x-1)^{2}}^{3-x}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}{|}_{(x-1)^{2}}^{x+1}\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}{|}_{(x-1)^{2}}^{3-x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[(x+1)^{2}-(x-1)^{4}]\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}[(3-x)^{2}-(x-1)^{4}]\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{(x+1)^{3}}{3}-\frac{(x-1)^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{1}+{[-\frac{(3-x)^{3}}{3}-\frac{(x-1)^{5}}{5}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =((\frac{8}{3}-0)-(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{5}))+((-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5})-(-\frac{8}{3}-0)) \\  & =\frac{32}{15}+\frac{32}{15} \\  & =\frac{64}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/648121ff2a676f6a472a6e221dffe813eca55f914aed0ca9a285bb0d4cd81ab3.png)

   

As a result, we get 

$$

$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 3}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}4xy\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}4xy\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}4xy\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}4xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}4xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[2x{y}^{2}]}_{1}^{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{[2x{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2x(9-1)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}2x(9-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}16x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}18x\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{x}^{2}{|}_{0}^{2}+9{x}^{2}{|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =8(4-0)+9(9-4) \\  & =77.\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curves $y= 2^x,$ $y=\sqrt{x}$  and lines $x=0$ and $y=2,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of a function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/b80527fdef6f890581b8f56431e1b72a8f7eae3b41827caa16486ed9f2fd45ea.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions $D_1$ and $D_2,$ as shown below.  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/939e46b3ed4266f3c18d3567f951276e420292781cfc414711c244f453bc4029.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
D_1 = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x  \leq 1, \quad \sqrt x \leq y \leq 2^x \big\}
$$

and 

$$
D_2 = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq x  \leq 4, \quad \sqrt x \leq y \leq 2 \big\}.
$$

 

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{{2}^{x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{4}{\int }_{\sqrt{x}}^{2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Representing a Double Integral as a Repeated Integral Over a Union of Type II Regions
canonical_examples.problem:
Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y=2+\ln x,$  and the lines $y=1$, $x=1,$ and  $x=e,$  as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/4b0dff15fa9fa93ed61183702bff6bb443daf14b0adbf56cf4b97e3bd830ceea.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2+\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,x={e}^{y-2}\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions $D_1$ and $D_2,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/2228ad860fea1e2c30d20bce749f654da02a97c65fd5e70152a07761e26f3e78.png)

    

As a result, we get

$$
D_1 = \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: 1 \leq y  \leq 2, \quad 1 \leq x \leq e \bigg\}
$$

and 

$$
D_2 = \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: 2 \leq y  \leq 3, \quad e^{y-2} \leq x \leq e\bigg\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{e}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{{e}^{y-2}}^{e}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/1d180fd5de88ebc465df522879142e5a4c5446c758aaccde792092968078c254.png)

The region $D$ is enclosed by the curves $x=2y^3-2y$ and  $x=y^3-4y,$ and the $y$-axis, as shown in the picture. Evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} \mathrm{d}A.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions $D_1$ and $D_2,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/6812e8036df171e162bee49d2edcff6d4a742e7bb4f14247713bd2332c64ccc6.png)

 

As a result, we get

$$
D_1 = \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: -2 \leq y  \leq 0, \quad 0 \leq x \leq y^3\!-\!4y \bigg\}
$$

and 

$$
D_2 = \bigg\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq y  \leq 1, \quad 2y^3\!-\!2y \leq x \leq 0 \bigg\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{3}-4y}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{2{y}^{3}-2y}^{0}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}[x]_{0}^{{y}^{3}-4y}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}[x]_{2{y}^{3}-2y}^{0}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}({y}^{3}-4y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}(2y-2{y}^{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{{y}^{4}}{4}-2{y}^{2}]}_{-2}^{0}+{[{y}^{2}-\frac{{y}^{4}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
